html:
The Shipibo-Konibo are a Panoan-speaking people of the Ucayali River in the Peruvian Amazon, some 30,000 strong. The Shipibo and Konibo were once separate groups, along with the Shetebo, and merged over time. They live along the river and its lakes, fishing and growing plantains and cassava, and many now live in the city of Pucallpa.

Their women make pottery and textiles covered with kené, dense geometric designs linked to songs and healing; Peru declared kené national cultural heritage in 2008. Shipibo healers are known for ayahuasca ceremonies, which now draw foreigners. Franciscan missionaries worked among them from the 1600s, and they suffered during the rubber boom. Their neighbours include the Kakataibo and the Asháninka, and they took in the last Iskonawa.
